questions.q: What is the first logical step when investigating a problem using the scientific method?
a: Making observations and identifying the problem

questions.q: Which of the following terms describes a possible explanation or educated guess that can be tested through experimentation?
During an experiment, what type of variable is purposely changed or manipulated by the experimenter?
Why is it important to keep all other conditions constant except the independent variable in a scientific experiment?
a: To make the experiment take longer to complete
To increase the cost of laboratory materials
To ensure that the results are due only to the variable being tested
To eliminate the need for recording any data

questions.q: What kind of data involves numbers, measurements, and quantities gathered during an investigation?
A student describes a leaf as being dark green with a smooth texture. What type of data is being recorded?
After analyzing experimental results, what is the next step a scientist normally takes?
a: Drawing a conclusion based on evidence

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of repeating an experiment multiple times?
a: To verify reliability and ensure results are not due to chance

questions.q: Which sense should never be used directly when identifying an unknown chemical substance in a science laboratory?
What is a well-tested and widely accepted explanation of a natural phenomenon supported by a vast body of evidence called?
What name is given to the factor that is measured or observed as a result of changes made in an experiment?
If an experiment's results do not support the original hypothesis, what should a student do?
a: Falsify the data to match the guess
Refine the hypothesis or form a new one based on the findings

questions.q: Which tool is most appropriate for recording precise temperature measurements of boiling water?
What is the main function of a control setup in a scientific experiment?
a: To provide a baseline for comparison against the experimental setup

questions.q: Which of the following actions represents a safe laboratory practice?
a: Tasting chemicals to check their purity
Running and playing around gas taps
Wiping up spills immediately and reporting accidents to the teacher

questions.q: When presenting numerical data clearly in a science report, which format is most effective for showing trends over time?
a: A well-labeled data table or line graph

questions.q: What is the term for information collected through the use of human senses or scientific instruments?
Why should laboratory apparatus such as measuring cylinders and beakers be handled with care?
a: They are made of expensive metals
They are often fragile and made of glass that can break easily
They rust when exposed to air

questions.q: A student notices that bread left in a warm, dark place grows mould faster than bread in a fridge. What is this initial statement an example of?
What is the ultimate goal of applying the scientific method in daily life and studies?
a: To memorize complex textbook definitions without thinking
To win prizes in school competitions
To create magic tricks for entertainment
To solve problems and understand natural phenomena logically

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a safety rule when heating a substance in a test tube?
a: Point the open end of the test tube away from yourself and others
Look directly down into the open tube while heating
Seal the top tightly with a cork during heating
Hold the glass tube directly with bare fingers

questions.q: What is an inference?
a: A direct measurement using a ruler
A logical conclusion or interpretation drawn from observations
A random guess with no supporting evidence

questions.q: Which of the following represents a quantitative observation?
a: The plant grew 5 centimeters in one week.

questions.q: What should you do immediately if chemical splashes into your eyes during a practical lesson?
a: Rub your eyes vigorously with dry hands
Cover your eyes with a cloth and wait
Ignore it and finish the experiment
Wash your eyes continuously with clean running water from an eyewash station or tap and inform the teacher

questions.q: Why must scientific reports be written clearly and honestly?
a: So other scientists can review, understand, and replicate the findings
To ensure nobody else can ever do the experiment
To make the notebook look colorful
To hide mistakes made during testing

questions.q: Which of the following describes a scientific law?
a: A temporary guess about a problem
A concise statement that summarizes a wide range of observations about a natural pattern without necessarily explaining why it happens
An opinion held by a famous scientist

questions.q: When plotting a line graph from an experiment, where is the independent variable conventionally placed?
What is the correct way to smell a chemical vapor in the laboratory?
a: Place your nose directly over the mouth of the boiling tube and inhale deeply
Heat the chemical until it vaporizes into the entire room
Taste a small drop of it first
Waft the fumes gently toward your nose with your hand from a safe distance

questions.q: What type of reasoning is used when specific observations are combined to arrive at a general conclusion or hypothesis?
Which equipment is best suited for measuring a precise volume of liquid such as 25.0 cm³ during an investigation?
a: A graduated measuring cylinder or pipette

questions.q: What is a primary characteristic of a well-designed scientific experiment?
a: Having multiple independent variables changing at the exact same time
Having no clear objective or hypothesis
Testing only one independent variable while keeping all other variables constant

questions.q: If a student wants to find out whether fertilizer type affects maize plant growth height, what is the dependent variable?
a: The height of the maize plants

questions.q: What is the purpose of wearing safety goggles in a science laboratory?
a: To protect the eyes from accidental chemical splashes, fumes, or flying debris
To improve vision in dark rooms
To look like a professional scientist

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes a hypothesis from a conclusion?
a: A hypothesis is tested after the experiment is finished.
A hypothesis is a proposed explanation tested before an experiment, whereas a conclusion is a final judgment based on the analyzed results.
A hypothesis is always a proven fact, while a conclusion is a guess.
There is no difference between them.

questions.q: Why are standard International System of Units (SI units) used in scientific investigations worldwide?
a: To make measurements more confusing for students
To ensure data can only be read in certain countries
To allow scientists around the world to communicate and compare measurements accurately
To increase the cost of laboratory equipment

questions.q: What should a student do with broken glassware in the laboratory?
a: Pick it up barehanded and throw it in the regular trash bin
Sweep it under the lab bench out of sight
Leave it for the next class to handle
Report it to the teacher immediately and dispose of it in a designated sharps or glass container

questions.q: Which process is part of critically evaluating scientific information found on the internet?
a: Checking the credibility of the source, looking for evidence, and verifying if experiments can be repeated
Believing every claim that sounds exciting
Ignoring all data that disagrees with personal opinions

questions.q: What is the function of a Bunsen burner in a school laboratory?
a: To provide a clean, adjustable flame for heating substances

questions.q: How can bias be minimized when conducting observations in a scientific study?
a: By changing data to fit what you want to happen
By observing only once and rushing away
By using objective measurement tools, clear criteria, and independent verification
By asking friends to guess the outcome

questions.q: What does a scientist do during the data analysis phase?
a: Organizes data into graphs or tables, calculates averages, and looks for patterns or relationships
